You are a programming expert. 
You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 

Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From da23be77e1292cd611e736c3aa17da633d7ddce7 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Paolo Abeni <pabeni@redhat.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Jun 2026 22:14:11 +1000
Subject: [PATCH] mptcp: allow subflow rcv wnd to shrink

In MPTCP connection, the `window` field in the TCP header refers to the
MPTCP-level rcv_nxt and it's right edge should not move backward. Such
constraint is enforced at DSS option generation time.

At the same time, the TCP stack ensures independently that the TCP-level
rcv wnd right's edge does not move backward. That in turn causes artificial
inflating of the MPTCP rcv window when the incoming data is acked at the
TCP level and is OoO in the MPTCP sequence space (or lands in the backlog).

As a consequence, the incoming traffic can exceed the receiver rcvbuf size
even when the sender is not misbehaving.

Prevent such scenario forcibly allowing the TCP subflow to shrink the
TCP-level rcv wnd regardless of the current netns setting.

Fixes: f3589be0c420 ("mptcp: never shrink offered window")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Paolo Abeni <pabeni@redhat.com>
Reviewed-by: Matthieu Baerts (NGI0) <matttbe@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Matthieu Baerts (NGI0) <matttbe@kernel.org>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260602-net-mptcp-misc-fixes-7-1-rc7-v2-4-856831229976@kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

diff --git a/net/mptcp/options.c b/net/mptcp/options.c
index 2d25f319f328..51ca334678b4 100644
--- a/net/mptcp/options.c
+++ b/net/mptcp/options.c
@@ -566,6 +566,7 @@ static bool mptcp_established_options_dss(struct sock *sk, struct sk_buff *skb,
 {
 	struct mptcp_subflow_context *subflow = mptcp_subflow_ctx(sk);
 	struct mptcp_sock *msk = mptcp_sk(subflow->conn);
+	struct tcp_sock *tp = tcp_sk(sk);
 	unsigned int dss_size = 0;
 	struct mptcp_ext *mpext;
 	unsigned int ack_size;
@@ -614,6 +615,12 @@ static bool mptcp_established_options_dss(struct sock *sk, struct sk_buff *skb,
 	if (dss_size == 0)
 		ack_size += TCPOLEN_MPTCP_DSS_BASE;
 
+	/* The caller is __tcp_transmit_skb(), and will compute the new rcv
+	 * wnd soon: ensure that the window can shrink.
+	 */
+	if (skb)
+		tp->rcv_wnd = tp->rcv_nxt - tp->rcv_wup;
+
 	dss_size += ack_size;
 
 	*size = ALIGN(dss_size, 4);
-- 
2.34.1

The patch modifies a single file: `net/mptcp/options.c`, specifically in the function `mptcp_established_options_dss`. The change adds a line that resets the TCP subflow’s receive window (`tp->rcv_wnd`) to the current difference between `rcv_nxt` and `rcv_wup` when an skb is present. This allows the subflow’s receive window to shrink, overriding the default TCP behavior that prevents window shrinkage.

The purpose of this fix is to address a bug where the MPTCP receive window could become artificially inflated. Inflation occurred when TCP-level ACKs for out-of-order (OoO) MPTCP data or data in the backlog caused the TCP window to remain large, while the MPTCP-level window was constrained not to shrink. This inflated window could exceed the receiver’s buffer size, even when the sender was not misbehaving. By forcibly allowing the subflow window to shrink in this context, the patch ensures the TCP window reflects the actual available buffer space, preventing potential buffer overflow and aligning with the intended MPTCP semantics.

The relationship between the modification and the bug is direct: the one-line change in the DSS option generation path corrects the window calculation to avoid the artificial inflation, thereby fixing the described performance/stability issue.

1. analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 
2. output the file name that is most likely to cause the bug. 



Provide a response strictly in the following format:
Root cause:<Root cause>
file:<file name>

Based on your summary and the commit message in the patch, you need to:

1. analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 
2. output the file name that is most likely to cause the bug. 



Provide a response strictly in the following format:
Root cause:<Root cause>
file:<file name>

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
<text>
// The following line is missing in the original code, causing the window to not shrink:
// tp->rcv_wnd = tp->rcv_nxt - tp->rcv_wup;
</text>
Reason:
Without this line, `tp->rcv_wnd` retains its previous value before calling `__tcp_transmit_skb()`. The TCP stack normally prevents the receive window from shrinking, but when TCP-level acknowledgement of out-of-order MPTCP data occurs, the window stays artificially large. This inflates the MPTCP-level receive window, allowing the sender to exceed the receiver's buffer capacity even without misbehavior.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
<text>
+	if (skb)
+		tp->rcv_wnd = tp->rcv_nxt - tp->rcv_wup;
</text>
Reason:
This assignment recalculates the subflow's receive window to the actual unacknowledged data size (`rcv_nxt - rcv_wup`) just before the TCP segment is transmitted. By doing so, the window can shrink to match the true available buffer space, preventing artificial inflation and keeping the received data within the receiver's buffer limits.
